official.deadline_central_display: Sunday, 1 November 2026 (registration deadline for Verfahren I-2027)
official.deadline_note: Alumni of Cusanuswerk study funding: complete applications by 1 February for the spring round and by 1 September for the autumn round. External applicants who miss the standard round can apply to the second round (Verfahren II-2027), which closes on Tuesday, 1 June 2027, with the selection decision in October 2027.
official.application_cycle: Verfahren I-2027 / Verfahren II-2027 (two selection rounds for external applicants)
official.status_note: Registrations for Verfahren I-2027 are open until 1 November 2026; the upload window stays open for a few days after the registration deadline, but late applications or documents cannot be considered.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Merkblatt states that, in addition to possible special funding of study and research stays abroad and conference visits, tuition fees (Studiengebühren) of up to 10,000 Euro per year of study can be supported on application; no blanket tuition coverage is published.
benefits: Doctoral stipend of EUR 1,750 per month, independent of parental income
Monthly research cost allowance of EUR 100 for materials and domestic travel costs
Child allowance of 155 Euro for the first and 50 Euro for each further child, with the possibility to convert funding time into child-care money, and a family supplement of 155 Euro where applicable
Health-insurance subsidy of 50 percent of premiums, up to a maximum of EUR 170 per month, where no compulsory statutory health insurance exists
Possible special funding of study and research stays abroad and of conference visits, and support of tuition fees of up to 10,000 Euro per year of study
Educational programme with retreats, exercises and encounter days plus the spiritual programme, and compatibility with positions of up to 25 percent of regular weekly working time
eligibility: Outstanding academic performance and inter- and transdisciplinary interest
Pronounced social responsibility, voluntary engagement, creativity, openness and capacity for reflection

Membership in the Catholic Church (applicants from non-united Orthodox or Oriental Orthodox churches may apply on individual review) and a lived Christian faith with willingness to co-shape the Church
Abitur or university entrance qualification entitling the applicant to study at a state or state-recognised university
German citizens: admission to doctoral study at a state-recognised university in Germany or abroad

Foreign applicants: admission to doctoral study at a state-recognised university in Germany and German at C1 minimum; applicants from developing or emerging countries in Africa, Asia, the Near and Middle East, Latin America and Eastern Europe are referred to the KAAD first, with a direct Cusanuswerk application only in exceptional cases confirmed by the KAAD
requirements: Register online in the OmniBuS portal and upload the complete application package by the registration deadline
Submit an exposé of the doctoral project (accepted in German or English)
Provide two substantive references from university teachers under § 42 Hochschulrahmengesetz
Read the Merkblatt for the doctoral scholarship before applying and check the contact person for the relevant subject group
documents: Exposé of the doctoral project with a timetable for the whole doctorate and the university's admission (a provisional supervision commitment by the supervisor suffices at application stage; admission must exist by the start of the scholarship)
Documents on academic performance and on the personal career path

Two references from university teachers per § 42 HRG, the first from the supervisor and the second from the co-supervisor, who must be independent of each other; interdisciplinary projects need references from all participating disciplines, and the signed and stamped forms can be sent directly to Auswahl-Prom@cusanuswerk.de

For doctorates abroad: a one-to-two-page justification of the chosen location; where the dissertation builds on a thesis (Diplom, Magister, Master or Staatsexamen), that thesis is uploaded in the 'Hausarbeit' category
selection_criteria: Internal review and first pre-selection based on all submitted documents, which usually takes at least four to six weeks

Two interviews for applicants not previously funded by the Cusanuswerk: one with a representative of the Catholic University Chaplaincy and one colloquium with a representative of the Cusanuswerk head office
Final decision by an interdisciplinary panel of university lecturers that also includes the Conference for Catholic University Chaplaincy (KHP) and the Cusanuswerk head office
coverage: Doctoral stipend of EUR 1,750 per month (Merkblatt: a stipend independent of parental income currently of 1,750 Euro monthly)
Monthly research cost allowance of EUR 100 for materials and domestic travel costs
Child and family supplements on application
Health-insurance subsidy of 50 percent of premiums, maximum EUR 170 per month, where no compulsory statutory health insurance exists
Study and research stays abroad and conference visits may be specially funded on application, as may tuition fees of up to EUR 10,000 per year of study
application_method: Register in the OmniBuS portal at https://omnibus.cusanuswerk.de/omnibus/register
Prepare the exposé, the references and the other documents before the registration deadline and upload them electronically
Wait for internal review and pre-selection, then attend the two interviews
Decision by the selection panel; candidates already funded in Cusanuswerk study funding register informally by e-mail to Auswahl-Prom@cusanuswerk.de
official.application_route: Online registration and document upload in the OmniBuS portal, followed by two interviews and an interdisciplinary panel decision
official.citizenship_residency: German citizens may be admitted to doctoral study in Germany or abroad; foreign applicants must be admitted to doctoral study at a state-recognised university in Germany, as funding of foreign doctoral candidates abroad is not possible
official.international_eligibility: Yes, for foreign applicants admitted to a doctorate at a state-recognised university in Germany with German at C1; applicants from developing or emerging countries are first referred to the KAAD
official.research_requirement: An exposé of the doctoral project must be submitted with the application, in German or English, containing a thematic outline of the planned dissertation, the current state of research and relevant literature, an explicit problem statement, the method, hypotheses and expected solutions, and a timetable for the whole doctorate, referring to the academic and methodological prerequisites on both sides
official.duration: Maximum funding period of three years and six months, with additional extension options for illness, maternity protection periods and child-rearing (the Merkblatt states doctoral funding of at most four years and six months)
official.description: The Cusanuswerk, the talent development body of the Catholic Church in Germany, funds doctoral candidates with a parent-independent stipend of EUR 1,750 per month plus a monthly research cost allowance of EUR 100 for a maximum of three years and six months, within an educational programme and a spare-time spiritual programme for members of the Catholic Church.
official.program_type: Church foundation scholarship for doctoral candidates (klassische Promotion)

not_confirmed: english_requirement (German at C1 is required for foreign applicants and no English test score is published)
verification.notes: Amount, monthly cadence, supplements, child and family allowances, the maximum funding period and the 1 November 2026 deadline confirmed on the official doctoral page; the Merkblatt of October 2026 confirms the monthly payment, the EUR 100 research allowance for materials and domestic travel costs, health-insurance subsidy rules, fee support of up to EUR 10,000 per year on application, the exposé and reference requirements, the two interviews and the extension rules.

applicant_utility.summary: Two facts decide most applications: Catholic Church membership is effectively a hard gate, and foreign applicants must already hold admission to doctoral study at a German university with German at C1, so start the admission procedure months before 1 November. The money is a stipend, not a fee award: 1,750 Euro per month plus 100 Euro research allowance, with tuition support of up to 10,000 Euro per year only on individual application. Budget for a long, staged process - internal review alone takes four to six weeks, then two interviews, then a panel.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Catholic doctoral candidates (or Cusanuswerk alumni) with an excellent degree, an interdisciplinary project and a concrete record of voluntary engagement.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the funding route first: Cusanuswerk alumni apply informally by e-mail, everyone else registers in OmniBuS for Verfahren I-2027 or II-2027
Obtain the university's admission, or at minimum a written supervision commitment that names the admission timeline
Ask the two reference holders under § 42 HRG to use the official reference form and to send it directly to Auswahl-Prom@cusanuswerk.de
Draft the exposé in German or English and include the timetable for the entire doctorate
Read the October 2026 Merkblatt and identify the contact person for your subject group in the downloads and info section
Register online well before 1 November 2026, since late applications or documents can no longer be considered
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly from a developing or emerging country, which is first referred to the KAAD rather than adjudicated by Cusanuswerk
Missing the church-membership condition or being unable to express a lived faith and willingness to co-shape the Church
Submitting an exposé without a timetable or without a clear problem statement, method and hypotheses
References from the same department where independence between the two reviewers cannot be shown
Interdisciplinary projects with references from only one discipline
Relying on a planned, not yet actual, admission right up to the start of the scholarship
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition above the EUR 10,000 per year that can be applied for, conference travel not approved on application, and any shortfall between the stipend and actual living and health-insurance costs (the insurance subsidy is capped at EUR 170 per month).
document_audit: The reference form is a separate download on the Cusanuswerk application pages, signed and stamped, and reviewed more favourably when sent directly by the reviewer
An English-language version of the reference form exists, which matters for supervisors abroad
The Personalbogen (personal data form) is easy to overlook because it sits separately from the exposé upload
If the dissertation builds on a Diploma, Magister, Master or Staatsexamen thesis, that thesis must be uploaded in the 'Hausarbeit' category
alerts: The upload window stays open only a few days after registration; technically being on time is what counts, not being almost on time
If Verfahren I-2027 (1 November 2026) is missed, the next chance is Verfahren II-2027, closing 1 June 2027 with decisions only in October 2027
Late funding starts are generally not possible, so align doctoral admission and the application round before registering
Doctoral funding is capped at three years and six months (four years six months including statutory extensions), so compute your timeline before you start
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in OmniBuS by 1 November, upload everything there, then internal review, two interviews and an interdisciplinary panel decision in March.
